The provided text aligns strongly with the conventions of the hardboiled detective and noir genres. By setting the narrative during Prohibition, it utilizes a historical backdrop that is frequently associated with moral ambiguity, lawlessness, and the rise of organized crime, all of which are staple elements of noir fiction. The protagonist, a "renowned detective," fits the archetype of the cynical or weary investigator common to the genre. Furthermore, the explicit mention of themes such as morality, corruption, and the pursuit of justice confirms the text's adherence to the genre-specific focus on ethical dilemmas and the flawed nature of society. There is no significant deviation from these established thematic norms; rather, the text serves as a quintessential example of noir storytelling.

The season that comes after autumn is winter.
